headline_marked: Google ad imagines Declaration of Independence [[written with AI]]
headline: Google ad imagines Declaration of Independence written with AI
summary: A new commercial from Google depicts the Founding Fathers using AI and Google Workspace tools to draft the Declaration of Independence, sparking mixed reactions online.
details: Google's latest commercial envisions a scenario where Thomas Jefferson, Ben Franklin, and other Founding Fathers utilize Google Workspace tools and AI to collaborate on the Declaration of Independence.

The ad showcases features like Google Docs for editing, Google Calendar for scheduling meetings, and Google Meet for remote discussions. AI tools like Gemini are depicted taking notes, and a "help me visualize" tool is used for conceptualizing the national seal.

The commercial, with the tagline "Group project, but make it 1776," has generated significant discussion. While YouTube and Instagram comments were largely positive, platforms like Bluesky saw criticism, with users calling the ad "cringey" and "tone deaf."

Some commentators noted that the ad's depiction of AI's role in historical collaboration is relatively subtle and avoids suggesting AI could improve the actual text of the Declaration. The video itself also exhibits visual characteristics often associated with AI-generated content.
Despite the mixed reception, the ad highlights Google's integration of AI into its productivity suite, prompting debate about the role of AI in creative and historical endeavors.

headline_marked: [[HTTP QUERY Method]] Solves Sending Request Bodies Safely in GET Requests (RFC 10008)
headline: HTTP QUERY Method Solves Sending Request Bodies Safely in GET Requests (RFC 10008)
summary: The new QUERY method (RFC 10008) combines POST's body support with GET's safety and cacheability, offering a significant architectural upgrade for web development.
details: The HTTP QUERY method, detailed in RFC 10008, addresses a long-standing challenge in web development: how to send complex request bodies in a way that is both safe and cacheable.

Traditionally, developers had to choose between GET (safe and cacheable but without a body) or POST (supports bodies but is not inherently safe or cacheable for retries). QUERY aims to bridge this gap.
Because QUERY is safe and idempotent, clients can automatically retry requests if network interruptions occur, without the risk of duplicating side effects. This adds significant architectural value.

The method combines the request body support of POST with the safety and cacheability features of GET. RFC 10008 mandates that caches incorporate both the request target and the body into their cache keys.

This new method is considered a true architectural upgrade, offering a more robust and efficient way to handle requests that require data payloads. Developers can consult the official specification for full details.
